correctness.rationale: Read the actual 2019 publisher article at Definition of coefficient direct sum, analysis and synthesis, Theorems 3.13 and 3.14, and the complete printed proof. For a one-block RFF A=I,v=2, S_R=4I; at f=1 the constraint f=4g forces g=1/4 and canonical a=S_R^-1 f=1/4. Its printed identity evaluates 1/16 on left and 1/4+9/16=13/16 on right; independently recalculated with exact fractions. The article actually proves sum v^2||a||^2=sum v^2<g,a>. Subtracting gives weighted orthogonality of a with g-a, hence the corrected weighted Pythagorean identity. In transformed coefficients h=v g, this is the ordinary canonical least-norm solution for the synthesis map. Finite scalar witness refutes the universal statement, and the Hilbert-space orthogonality supplies the general correction subject to the original frame/Bessel hypotheses.

value.rationale: A published reconstruction/minimum-norm theorem is false under its actual advertised arbitrary positive weights. The scalar witness isolates the error without artificial parameter restrictions and the general weighted identity supplies the correct canonical coefficient geometry for relay synthesis. This has clear substantive consequences when comparing nonuniform communication-channel weights; it is not merely a cosmetic normalization complaint.

final_claim: Hong--Li Theorem 3.14 is false for arbitrary positive relay weights: a single complex scalar block with weight 2 gives 1/16 versus 13/16. The correct Pythagorean minimal-coefficient identity uses the weighted norm sum v_ij^2||g_ij||^2.
limitations: No claim that other 2019 theorems are false.
